title: Maintainability Ops Playbook: Rotation, Escalation, and Communications
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents Redwood Inference's operational approach to maintainability-focused incidents — the class of events where service correctness is intact but performance, cost, or sustainable operations are at risk (examples: sustained cache thrash, KV-store growth causing OOM risk, inefficient batch behavior causing cost spikes). The goal is to help responders quickly stabilize, execute corrective actions, and communicate internally and to customers with transparency.

Scope: Applies to all inference-serving services and orchestration components for hosted and dedicated fleets. This complements the incident-first runbooks (latency/outage) and is oriented toward prevention, controlled mitigation, and planned remediation workstreams.

Ownership and Roles

- Bridge Coordinator (BC): primary point for incident orchestration during maintainability events. Typically an SRE or senior platform engineer.
- Service Owner (SO): product/engineering team responsible for the impacted service.
- Runtime Specialist (RS): engineer with deep knowledge of the serving runtime and kernel selection layer.
- Capacity & Cost Lead (CCL): owner for quota/capacity decisions and reserved capacity adjustments.
- Communications Lead (CL): writes internal updates and customer-facing messages.
- Incident Reporter (IR): person who opened the incident, responsible for initial context and artifacts.

SLOs and Thresholds (Maintainability Class)

- Cost spike alert: >35% increase in inference cost sustained over 30 minutes vs 7-day baseline -> P2 track.
- KV cache growth: persistent >80% mem utilization for model-worker KV cache for 15+ minutes -> P2.
- Batch inefficiency: average token-per-request drop below baseline leading to >20% per-token cost increase over 30 minutes -> P2.
- Slow-degradation (latency tail): 95th percentile latency moving >2x baseline but <4x (no clear outage) -> P2.

If a maintainability incident crosses into outage criteria (errors >1% or 95th latency >4x baseline and customer impact), escalate to P1 incident flow (see related pages).

Detection and Triage

1. Automated detection sources
   - Cost monitors (Billing pipeline alerts)
   - Prometheus rule alerts for KV mem use and batch size distribution
   - Tracing-based heuristics detecting excessive re-batching or cache-miss ratios
   - Customer tickets indicating cost regressions

2. Initial triage checklist (BC or oncall):
   - Capture scope: affected models, regions, tenant types (hosted/dedicated/private).
   - Determine classification: maintainability vs correctness/outage.
   - Assign roles: name BC, SO, RS, CCL, CL.
   - Create incident channel (Slack) and a short incident page stub.

Short incident page stub template (create in Incidents space)

Title: [Maintainability] <Service> - <Short problem> - YYYY-MM-DD
Severity: P2
Owner: <BC name>
Status: Triaging
Impact summary: <one-sentence>
Initial hypothesis: <one-sentence>
Actions in progress: <bullets>

Stabilization Runbook (first 60 minutes)

Goal: Stop immediate resource or cost bleed and buy time for investigation.

1) Limit surface area
   - If the problem is tenant-specific, throttle tenant(s) by applying rate-limit profile: CLI example:
     curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://admin.redwood/api/v1/limits -d '{ "tenant": "<tenant-id>", "rate": 0.1 }'
   - For global cost spikes, enable emergency batching limiter: set batch_max_tokens to 1024 and batch_timeout_ms to 5.

2) Apply safe-fallback model routing
   - Route affected traffic to a quantized-friendly variant (e.g., model-v2-quant) that preserves correctness while lowering runtime memory pressure. Update routing policy: 
     redwood routing apply --service <svc> --route emergency-quant-variant

3) Temporary capacity change
   - If memory growth threatens OOMs, add a warm standby node pool via autoscaler override (SRE permission required):
     kubectl scale deployment <worker-pool> --replicas=<current+2> -n inference

4) Short-term cost cap
   - Set per-tenant spend cap for 2 hours in billing control panel, if available; otherwise ask CCL to flag for manual throttling.

Investigation (60–240 minutes)

- Gather telemetry:
  - Traces showing KV hit/miss ratio, token-per-request distribution, batch occupancy histograms.
  - Metrics to collect: kv_cache_utilization, kv_eviction_rate, batch_fill_rate, tokens_generated_per_request, per-token-cost_estimated.
- Hypothesis pivot table (note each hypothesis with evidence vs counter-evidence).
- Typical root causes to evaluate:
  - Regression in compilation/kernel selection causing larger memory working sets.
  - Changes to prompt templates increasing prefix length and evicting KV caches.
  - New model variant rolled without quantization profile.
  - Workload shift: more single-token inference requests (inefficient batching).

Mitigation and Remediation (4 hours onward)

Remediation choices (depending on root cause):
- Kernel/compile rollback: revert recent runtime compile flags or kernel bundle. Follow runtime rollback playbook.
- Prompt-level mitigation: apply prefix-capping proxy that trims user-provided system prompts >N tokens (configurable per-tenant).
- Batch tuning: adjust batching weight heuristics to coalesce small requests (increase batch_timeout_ms to 10–15 ms, allow slightly higher latency for cost win).
- Long-term model variant changes: schedule a canary rollout with lower memory footprint and persistent KV cache strategy.

Post-incident Workstreams

- Postmortem: complete within 3 business days with an owner assigned. Use structure: Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root Cause, Contributing Factors, Mitigation, Remediation Plan, Action Items (owner + due date).
- Remediation backlog: create Jira epic tagged "maintainability-<service>-YYYYMM" for code changes, runtime improvements, and monitoring gaps.
- Telemetry enhancement: add new alerts for early warning at 10–15 minute windows with less aggressive thresholds.

On-call Rotations and Handoffs

- Rotation length: 1 week for SRE oncall, 2-week rotation for BC oncall (primary incident coordinator).
- Handoff template (Slack and doc):
  - Current incidents and statuses
  - Paging quiet windows and scheduled maintenance
  - Known noisy alerts and mitigations in place
  - Any active runbooks or experimental automation toggles

- Shadowing & ramp: new oncall engineers must complete two supervised shifts and one game-day exercise focusing on maintainability scenarios before being primary.

Game-day Scenarios (quarterly)

Objective: practice early-detection and controlled mitigation for maintainability incidents without customer-impacting outages. Run three scenarios each quarter:
1) KV cache growth due to model change (simulate by toggling mem pressure in staging).
2) Sudden workload shift to single-token requests (create synthetic requests).
3) Compilation regression causing higher memory usage on a subset of nodes.

During each game day: measure time to detection, time to stabilization (throttling/routing), and time to mitigation (remediation applied). Record lessons and update runbooks within 5 business days.

Status Page and Customer Communications

Status page taxonomy:
- Operational: No customer-facing impact.
- Degraded: Potential for increased latency/cost but no correctness loss.
- Partial outage: measurable customer success/regression for subset.
- Major outage: broad customer impact.

Customer-facing template (Degraded)

Subject: Redwood Inference - Degraded performance for <service> in <region>

Hi <customer-name>,

We are investigating a performance degradation affecting <service> in <region>. During this time, you may experience increased response times or higher-than-normal inference costs. No correctness errors have been observed. Our team has applied temporary routing and throttling to stabilize the service and is actively investigating the root cause.

What we are doing:
- Routing traffic to a lower-memory variant while we investigate
- Temporarily limiting burst capacity for affected tenants where needed
- Performing telemetry analysis and scheduling targeted remediation

Estimated next update: in 60 minutes. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or open a support ticket.

Thank you for your patience,
The Redwood Inference Operations Team

Internal status update (Slack announcement example)

[INCIDENT] Maintainability - <service> - Degraded performance (P2)
BC: @<name> | SO: @<name> | RS: @<name>
Summary: Elevated KV cache use causing cost-pressure. Temporary routing to quantized variant applied.
Next update: in 30 minutes.

Status page JSON payload (example for automation)

POST https://status.redwood.example/api/v1/incidents
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY

Payload:
{
  "name": "Degraded performance: <service> in <region>",
  "status": "degraded",
  "impact": "Users may see higher latency and increased cost for inference; no correctness regressions observed",
  "components": ["<service>-api", "<service>-runtime"],
  "started_at": "2027-02-10T14:12:00Z",
  "updates": [ { "body": "Temporary routing to quantized variant applied; investigation ongoing", "timestamp": "2027-02-10T14:20:00Z" } ]
}

(Automations should redact tenant IDs from public payloads; internal tickets should include full tenant-scoped context.)

Postmortem Requirements

- Template fields (all as text):
  - Title, Incident ID, Severity, Start/End times, Impact summary, Affected customers (anonymized), Root Cause, Timeline, Mitigation steps, Remediation plan, Action items (owner & due date).
- Publish cadence: draft within 72 hours; final publish after review and verification of remediation (no later than 30 days).

Runbook Governance and Maintenance

- Runbooks updated: after any game-day or live incident with time-to-update <= 5 business days.
- Runbook owner: SO or BC for the service. Runbook review: quarterly.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets and dashboards

- List active batch profiles:
  redwood batch profiles list --service <svc>
- Inspect KV cache metrics (Prometheus query):
  max_over_time(kv_cache_utilization{service="<svc>"}[30m])
- Re-route traffic to emergency variant:
  redwood routing apply --service <svc> --route emergency-quant-variant --description "Maintainability emergency"
- Create temporary spend cap (billing UI quick link): https://billing.redwood.example/tenants/<tenant-id>/caps

Contacts and Escalation Matrix

- Engineering SRE Pager: #sre-pager (Slack) and PagerDuty 
- Emergency Exec escalation: Oncall Lead -> Head of Platform -> CTO (only for broad customer-impacting events)
